clips.send: Etowah Mounds (Cartersville). A 54-acre town with six mounds, a plaza and a defensive ditch and palisade; several thousand people lived here. The 63-ft mound probably held the chief’s or priest’s house. Famous finds include a pair of painted marble statues and copper plates showing bird-like dancers. Many historians think this was Itaba, a town de Soto passed in August 1540.

clips.send: Dont mix up: The bow and arrow arrived in the Woodland period — Archaic hunters used the atlatl (spear-thrower). Mounds didn’t start with the Mississippians: Woodland people built burial mounds; Mississippians built flat-topped “platform mounds” with temples or chiefs’ houses on top. Memory hook: “Paleo spear, Archaic atlatl, Woodland bow, Mississippian corn.”

clips.send: Europeans brought smallpox, measles and other diseases Native people had never met. Within a few years of de Soto’s visit, the powerful chiefdoms began to collapse — archaeologists see disease as a major cause. Many towns lost most of their people; survivors regrouped into the Creek and Cherokee societies of later times.

clips.send: 16 世纪末到 17 世纪，西班牙方济各会修士在瓜莱人，Guale，的海岛上建立传教站，最重要的是圣凯瑟琳斯岛上的圣卡塔利娜·德瓜莱。原住民被要求改信天主教、为传教站和圣奥古斯丁劳动并缴纳玉米。1597 年瓜莱人起义，焚毁了传教站。1680 年，受卡罗来纳英国人武装的韦斯托人袭击后，传教站被迫南撤。

clips.send: 圣卡塔利娜·德瓜莱（圣凯瑟琳斯岛）。西班牙在佐治亚海岸瓜莱人中设立的主要传教站。 1597 年瓜莱人起义时被焚毁，1605 年方济各会重建，1680 年遭袭后被放弃。 考古学家在 20 世纪 80 年代重新发现了这座失落的传教站。
